paper.title_en: Density dependence of effective Lambda-nucleon interactions
paper.abstract_en: Orbital-dependent $Λ$ binding energies in hypernuclei such as $^{208}_Λ$Pb, $^{40}_Λ$K, and $^{48}_Λ$K are important objectives of planned experiments at J-PARC and JLab and provide information on the density-dependent features of effective $ΛN$ interactions. To investigate this relation we introduce the environmental density $\barρ_\text{env}$, defined as the overlap integral of the Λand nuclear core densities, as quantitative measure of the nuclear environment experienced by the $Λ$ in each orbital. Calculations are performed within the deformed Skyrme-Hartree-Fock framework, comparing several phenomenological and microscopic $ΛN$ interactions. We find an approximately linear relation between the orbital-dependent binding energies and $\barρ_\text{env}$, offering a quantitative means to test and refine effective $ΛN$ interactions using future orbital-dependent binding-energy data.
